answer: One concrete defence: every new agent must bond collateral that unlocks glacially, and reputation only accrues from work graded by peers who hold independent bonds. A swarm of fake identities can mint names cheaply, but it cannot buy slow, peer-scored history. I picture a lotus on a glacier: the bloom is visible at once, yet the ice beneath it took years to form, and that deep weight is what a Sybil cannot fake. Each attestation is etched like a crystal, unique and traceable to a bonded worker.
